summary:
### TL;DR
- **CodeQL 2.27.4** is rolling out automatically on github.com. It removes the `CWE-730` tag from about 20 ReDoS and regex-injection queries across C#, Java/Kotlin, JS/TS, Python, Ruby and Swift. It also adds a symlink check when you bundle or publish packs. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))
- **GitHub Docs has deprecated GHES 3.18.** Content gated to "GHES > 3.18" now applies to all documented versions. This includes OIDC colon-encoding in `sub` claims, push protection pattern configuration, Dependabot metrics, `cooldown` and extended schedule intervals. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/92ac1df470eeb313eac8fc94002315b3781c975c))
- **Dependabot `reviewers` guidance is gone from the docs.** Use CODEOWNERS to auto-assign reviewers. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/customizing-dependabot-prs))

### Action required
- **Review anything that filters by `CWE-730`.** This includes dashboards, alert filters, SARIF post-processing and compliance mappings. These queries no longer carry the tag: `cs/redos`, `cs/regex-injection`, `java/redos`, `java/polynomial-redos`, `java/regex-injection`, `js/redos`, `js/polynomial-redos`, `js/regex-injection`, `js/regex-injection-more-sources`, `js/server-crash`, `js/loop-bound-injection`, `py/redos`, `py/polynomial-redos`, `py/regex-injection`, `rb/redos`, `rb/polynomial-redos`, `rb/regexp-injection`, `swift/redos`, `swift/regex-injection`. The change is live on github.com now. It will ship in GHES 3.24. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))
- **Check CodeQL packs that use symlinks.** When you bundle or publish a pack, the CLI now omits files whose symlinks resolve outside the pack root and shows a warning. Make sure your packs don't depend on such files. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))
- **GHES 3.18 users:** documentation for 3.18 has been deprecated. No date is given in the source. Plan your upgrade path accordingly. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/92ac1df470eeb313eac8fc94002315b3781c975c))
- **Move off the Dependabot `reviewers` option.** The docs previously warned that `reviewers` "is closing down and will be removed in a future release" of GHES. That fallback section has now been removed, and CODEOWNERS is the documented method. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/manage-your-dependency-security/customizing-dependabot-security-prs))

### Security improvements
- **Safer CodeQL pack publishing.** The CLI validates that every file stays inside the pack root after symlinks are resolved. This prevents accidental inclusion of files from outside the pack. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))
- **Better Java/Kotlin coverage with fewer false positives.**
  - `java/log-injection` now recognizes sanitizers from the JDK, Apache Commons Lang/Text, Guava, OWASP Java Encoder and Spring.
  - Path-injection queries recognize more guard and string-replacement operations from Commons Lang and Guava.
  
  ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))
- **Fewer false positives in Rust and C/C++.**
  - Rust: `rust/uncontrolled-allocation-size`, `rust/log-injection` and `rust/cleartext-logging`.
  - C/C++: `cpp/suspicious-pointer-scaling` ignores `std::byte*` arithmetic, and the unused-variable queries respect `[[maybe_unused]]`.
  
  ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))
- **Cleaner CLI output for automation.** JVM warnings and initialization errors now go to stderr, so JSON and other machine-readable output on stdout is no longer polluted. This is relevant for Actions workflows that parse CLI output. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-04-codeql-2-27-4-improves-accuracy-and-query-metadata))

### Docs changes worth reading
All of these come from the GHES 3.18 deprecation commit. The guidance below now applies to every documented version, not just newer ones.

- **OIDC reference.** The "Filtering for metadata containing `:`" section is now unconditional. Any `:` in metadata values is encoded as `%3A` in the `sub` claim, for example `repo:octo-org/octo-repo:environment:Production%3AV1`. Check your cloud trust policies if environment names contain colons. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc))
- **Push protection for generic patterns.** The docs now state unconditionally that generic patterns, such as private keys and connection strings, must also be enabled in the org or enterprise push protection pattern configuration.
  - Push protection concept: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/secret-security/push-protection)
  - Org settings: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/establish-complete-coverage/configure-global-settings)
  - Enterprise settings: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-enterprise-security/establish-complete-coverage/configure-additional-settings)
- **Supported secret scanning patterns.** The generic `ec_private_key` pattern (High precision) is now listed without a version gate. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/secret-security/supported-secret-scanning-patterns))
- **Dependabot options.** `cooldown` and the extended `schedule.interval` values (`quarterly`, `semiannually`, `yearly`, `cron`) are documented for all versions. Note that `cooldown` applies to version updates, not security updates.
  - Options reference: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference)
  - Optimizing PR creation: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/optimizing-pr-creation-version-updates)
- **Dependabot metrics and vulnerability exposure.** These pages are no longer feature-gated and now apply to fpt, GHEC and GHES. The Dependabot dashboard filters are also documented unconditionally.
  - Viewing metrics: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/view-and-interpret-data/analyze-organization-data/viewing-metrics-for-dependabot-alerts)
  - Prioritizing alerts: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/manage-security-alerts/prioritizing-dependabot-alerts-using-metrics)
  - Vulnerability exposure: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/vulnerability-reporting-and-management/vulnerability-exposure)
  - Dashboard filters: [docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/security-at-scale/overview-dashboard-filters)

changelog.title: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves accuracy and query metadata
changelog.text: CodeQL is the static analysis engine behind GitHub code scanning, which finds and remediates security issues in your code. We’ve recently released CodeQL 2.27.4 with query accuracy improvements across several languages, stronger security checks when you bundle or publish a pack, and corrections to query metadata. Query changes Java/Kotlin The java/log-injection query now recognizes additional sanitizers and sanitizer guards from the JDK, Apache Commons Lang and Text, Guava, OWASP Java Encoder, and Spring Framework. Path-injection queries now recognize additional substring guards and string replacement and removal operations from Apache Commons Lang and Guava. Rust We have reduced false positives in the rust/uncontrolled-allocation-size , rust/log-injection , and rust/cleartext-logging queries. C/C++ The cpp/suspicious-pointer-scaling query no longer reports intentional pointer arithmetic on std::byte* buffers. The cpp/unused-local-variable and cpp/unused-static-variable queries no longer report variables marked with [[maybe_unused]] . CWE metadata changes CodeQL no longer applies the CWE-730 tag to the following queries: C# : cs/redos and cs/regex-injection . Java/Kotlin : java/redos , java/polynomial-redos , and java/regex-injection . JavaScript/TypeScript : js/redos , js/polynomial-redos , js/regex-injection , js/regex-injection-more-sources , js/server-crash , and js/loop-bound-injection . Python : py/redos , py/polynomial-redos , and py/regex-injection . Ruby : rb/redos , rb/polynomial-redos , and rb/regexp-injection . Swift : swift/redos and swift/regex-injection . This was initially reported in CodeQL issue #22318 ; thank you to @wiggin15 for the feedback. CodeQL CLI The CLI now writes Java virtual machine warnings and initialization errors to standard error, so they won’t interfere with JSON or other machine-readable output. When you bundle or publish a pack, the CLI checks whether each file remains inside the pack root after resolving symbolic links. It omits files that resolve outside the root and displays a warning. For full details, see the CodeQL 2.27.4 changelog . GitHub automatically deploys every new CodeQL version to users of GitHub code scanning on github.com. The new functionality in CodeQL 2.27.4 will also be included in the GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) 3.24 release. If you use an older version of GHES, you can manually upgrade your CodeQL version . The post CodeQL 2.27.4 improves accuracy and query metadata appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot is now available in Xcode’s coding assistant
changelog.text: You can now work with GitHub Copilot directly in Xcode’s built-in coding assistant , bringing Copilot into your native Xcode workflow. The integration is now in public preview, available starting with Xcode 27.3 beta. This gives you another way to use Copilot in Xcode. The existing GitHub Copilot for Xcode extension remains a separate option, so you can choose the workflow that works best for you. Get started Download Xcode 27.3 beta from Apple Developer Downloads . You’ll need a Mac running macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later. In Xcode, open Xcode > Settings > Intelligence to set up GitHub Copilot in the coding assistant. For more information, see Setting up coding intelligence and the Xcode 27.3 beta release notes . All Copilot plans are supported. Share your feedback Help us improve the experience by sharing your feedback in the GitHub Copilot for Xcode repository or through Apple Feedback Assistant . The post GitHub Copilot is now available in Xcode’s coding assistant appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
